rationale: Followed the open item of the store-failure account into the vote path, which the account had left as an inference. Both sides of a vote exchange read the node's in-memory last log rather than its log store: the handler that decides whether to grant reads the last index and term from the state, and a node that campaigns builds its RequestVote from the same two fields, so a node whose store lost a suffix it still claims solicits votes with a log its store cannot back. I recorded that as a behavior entry with two new source anchors, and narrowed the question's discriminator so the remaining work is the live leader's retry walk and this vote consequence, which is still source-read rather than measured.

investigations.discriminator: A live leader replicating to a follower whose store failed inside the truncation window: the leader's nextIndex for that peer over the following interval and whether its rejections walk it down to the start of the log, whether the follower then accepts anything before a snapshot is installed, and, while the state persists, the last log index and term the follower offers in a RequestVote and whether it grants a vote to a candidate whose log matches the store rather than its own stale claim.

knowledge.statement: A node judges and claims elections with its in-memory last log, never with a fresh read of the log store. The vote handler takes the last index and term from the state's last log - the last stored index and term, or the snapshot's when the snapshot is newer - and refuses the request when that term is greater than the candidate's, or when the terms are equal and that index is greater; the campaign path builds its RequestVote from the same two fields. Both fields are written only by setLastLog on the stored path, so a node whose AppendEntries handler deleted a suffix and then aborted before storing the replacement offers and defends a log entry its store no longer holds, and can refuse a grant to a candidate whose log is at least as complete as the store it actually has.
knowledge.conditions: Any vote exchange on a node whose in-memory last log and log store disagree, which the aborted-append state produces when the suffix was deleted and the replacement was not stored; the same fields feed the candidacy claim of a node that campaigns while in that state.
